cues.text: A playground has a corner cut out for a tree. Can we still work out how many paving tiles it needs? An irregular outline does not stop us measuring. Let us turn the tricky shape into familiar rectangles.
cues.asr_text: A PLAYGROUND HAS A CORNER CUT OUT FOR A TREE CAN WE STILL WORK OUT HOW MANY PAVING TILES IT NEEDS AN IRREGULAR OUTLINE DOES NOT STOP US MEASURING LET US TURN THE TRICKY SHAPE INTO FAMILIAR RECTANGLES

cues.text: Success criteria. I can split a shape or subtract a missing rectangle. I can check every outside length for perimeter. I can compare designs using the required measure.
board: 1. Split a shape or subtract a missing rectangle.
2. Check every outside length for perimeter.
3. Compare designs using the required measure.
cues.asr_text: SUCCESS CRITERIA I CAN SPLIT A SHAPE OR SUBTRACT A MISSING RECTANGLE I CAN CHECK EVERY OUTSIDE LENGTH FOR PERIMETER I CAN COMPARE DESIGNS USING THE REQUIRED MEASURE

board_events.text: 1. Split a shape or subtract a missing rectangle.
2. Check every outside length for perimeter.
3. Compare designs using the required measure.

cues.text: Build an L shape with square tiles, then slide a pencil along possible dividing lines. You can split its area into non-overlapping rectangles, or start with a large rectangle and subtract the missing part. Both methods must cover exactly the same surface.
cues.asr_text: BUILD AN L SHAPE WITH SQUARE TILES THEN SLIDE A PENCIL ALONG POSSIBLE DIVIDING LINES YOU CAN SPLIT ITS AREA INTO NON OVERLAPPING RECTANGLES OR START WITH A LARGE RECTANGLE AND SUBTRACT THE MISSING PART BOTH METHODS MUST COVER EXACTLY THE SAME SURFACE

cues.text: An L-shaped space fits inside an eight-metre by six-metre rectangle. A three-metre by two-metre corner is missing. Predict whether its area is greater or smaller than forty-eight square metres.
cues.asr_text: AN L SHAPED SPACE FITS INSIDE AN EIGHT METRE BY SIX METER RECTANGLE A THREE METRE BY TWO METRE CORNER IS MISSING PREDICT WHETHER ITS AREA IS GREATER OR SMALLER THAN FORTY EIGHT SQUARE METRES

cues.text: Subtract the missing six square metres from forty-eight. The L-shaped area is forty-two square metres. As a check, split it into an eight-by-four rectangle and a five-by-two rectangle. Thirty-two plus ten also gives forty-two.
cues.asr_text: SUBTRACT THE MISSING SIX SQUARE METERS FROM FORTY EIGHT THE L SHAPED AREA IS FORTY TWO SQUARE METERS AS ITS CHECK SPLIT IT INTO AN EIGHT BY FOUR RECTANGLE AND A FIVE BY TWO RECTANGLE THIRTY TWO PLUS TEN ALSO GIVES FORTY TWO

cues.text: A larger design fits inside a ten-metre by eight-metre rectangle, with a four-by-three corner missing. Plan the area calculation first. Keep the border measurement separate from the surface measurement.
cues.asr_text: A LARGER DESIGN FITS INSIDE AT TEN METER BY EIGHT METRE RECTANGLE WITH A FOUR BY THREE CORNER MISSING PLANT THE AREA CALCULATION FIRST KEEP THE BORDER MEASUREMENT SEPARATE FROM THE SURFACE MEASUREMENT

cues.text: The usable area is sixty-eight square metres. For its border, trace ten, five, four, three, six and eight metres. That perimeter is thirty-six metres. Different questions about the same design need different measures.
cues.asr_text: THE USUAL AREA IS SIXTY EIGHT SQUARE METRES FOR ITS BORDER TRACE TEN FIVE FORTY SIX AND EIGHT METRES THAT PERIMETER IS THIRTY SIX METRES DIFFERENT QUESTIONS ABOUT THE SAME DESIGN NEED DIFFERENT MEASURES

cues.text: Using the full eight-by-six rectangle would include the tree corner. That overcounts six square metres. Subtract the missing rectangle, or add two rectangles that cover only the actual playground.
cues.chapter: The missing corner does not need tiles
cues.asr_text: USING THE FULL EIGHT BY SIX RECTANGLE WOULD INCLUDE THE TREE CORNER THAT OVERCOUNTS SIX SQUARE METERS SUBTRACT THE MISSING RECTANGLE OR ADD TWO RECTANGLES THAT COVER ONLY THE ACTUAL PLAYGROUND

cues.text: A six-by-five rectangle has a two-by-two corner removed. What area remains? Look at the model, and keep your prediction in mind.
cues.asr_text: AS SIX BY FIVE RECTANGLE HAS A TWO BY TWO CORNER REMOVED WHAT AREA REMAINS LOOK AT THE MODEL AND KEEP YOUR PREDICTION IN MIND

cues.text: Thirty minus four leaves twenty-six square units. The missing corner is not part of the surface, so subtract it once, rather than including the full bounding rectangle.
cues.asr_text: THIRTY MINUS FAR LEAVES TWENTY SIX SQUARE UNITS THE MISSING CORNER IS NOT PART OF THE SURFACE SO SUBTRACT AT ONCE RATHER THAN INCLUDING THE FULL BOUNDING RECTANGLE

cues.text: Choose the measure the problem needs. For area, split or subtract rectangles; for perimeter, trace every outside edge. Draw a garden on squared paper and explain a paving plan and a fencing plan. Check that your answers describe the actual design. Reflect on which model helped you and why. Now try the MathMagic practice, and explain your thinking to someone.
board: Plan, calculate and check the real design.
